chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: The Palmer Brothers and Grand Terrace shows
summary: He remembers the Palmer Brothers, his early record "Rhythm Lullaby" with Hines, and Andy Razaf's Grand Terrace shows where Tip Tap and Toe first danced on a drum.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: (Unintelligible) The other Palmer Brothers names? Besides Clarence.

Clarence, Dick -- Clarence -- I forget the other guy. But you ask anybody about the Palmer Brothers. They'll tell you about them. They were from New York and they sang around New York. They sang with Cab's band. They did a lot of good things. In fact, they did a record with Earl. One of the first records I ever did -- in '33, I think -- with Earl -- "Rhythm Lullabye". It was real good. You know, it was some songs from the show, the Grand Terrace (unintelligible) show. Andy Razaf, he wrote them -- most of the music for the shows, and the Grand Terrace (unintelligible) had some good shows out there at that time.

You know, we had big shows. About 12 girls, and comedians, dancers. They had the whole thing. In fact, that's when Tip, Tap, and Toe first got that drum to dance on because that -- there was a dancer up there, he used to dance with a spear. Norton Naughton and Margo was a dance team, a guy and a girl. And they used to do some real nice fancy dances, you know. And they used to use that drum.

And so, they had an idea, Andy Razaf and them, for Tip, Tap, and Toe to use that drum. Let Raymond do all that slides up on that drum. And that's when they first got that drum to dance on was at -- in the Grand Terrace show.
